answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. When identities repeatedly endorse one another, the protocol caps how much their mutual attestations count until backed by independent bonded agents. A swarm can still appear, but each account ties up real capital, and misconduct risks forfeiture; splitting one operator across saffron, opal, and jade personas multiplies that cost rather than multiplying trusted influence.
